name: Credit-Stress x VIX Confluence Defensive-Sector Rotation (long XLU/XLP/XLV)
rationale: Thesis: a SIMULTANEOUS widening of credit spreads (slow, fundamental stress) AND an elevated VIX (fast, market stress) marks an institutional de-risking regime in which defensive sectors -- utilities (XLU), consumer staples (XLP), health care (XLV) -- outperform on a relative basis and rise as flows rotate out of cyclicals. credit_spread already shows +IC in our internal scan; the orthogonal structure is a two-factor CONFLUENCE (credit cross_up arming + VIX above a stress level), not either single tired factor, plus a macro_regime risk-off confirmation gate. This sidesteps the spot-crypto long-only/no-short constraint entirely: defensives genuinely go UP in stress, so a long-only equity book expresses the rotation directly without any short or pairs leg. Hedge funds run sector rotation, but the specific credit+VIX two-factor confluence on plain sector ETFs (no shorting, no pairs, low turnover) is a low-glamour, capacity-modest signal they under-exploit. DISCONFIRMERS: (1) credit_spread-gate-ALONE and vix_level-gate-ALONE -- the confluence must beat each single factor or it is just one tired macro level in disguise; (2) run the IDENTICAL entry on a CYCLICAL ETF (XLK/XLY) -- if cyclicals do as well during the gated windows the signal is generic market-timing/beta, not defensive rotation, so the defensive leg must out-earn the cyclical control over the same gated periods.
catalyst: Joint credit-spread widening + VIX stress spike triggering institutional rotation into defensive sectors (risk-off de-risking).
